newsitem.title: ESTONIA: NO CHANGE TO ECONOMIC POLICY BY NEW GOVT - FINMIN.
newsitem.headline: NO CHANGE TO ECONOMIC POLICY BY NEW GOVT - FINMIN.

text.p: Estonia's Finance Minister Mart Opmann said on Thursday that the country's economic policy would continue unchanged under the new government currently being formed by Mart Siimann.
Opmann said he was 99 percent certain that he would remain finance minister in the new government that will be presented to the president by Siimann next week.
"As for economic policy, we are going to carry on the same principles quite closely as the former government," Opmann told Reuters in an interview.
He said the new government would continue to run an open liberal economic policy, balanced budget and retain the currency board that pegs the kroon against the mark at eight to one.
"These are the columns of economic reform of our economic policy and number four is structural reform. We are going to contiune these principles," Opmann said.
Siimann was on Wednesday given the approval of parliament to form a government to replace that of Tiit Vaehi who stepped down last month after narrowly winning a parliament no-confidence vote.

Opmann dismissed statistics showing there was less foreign investment in Estonia compared to 1994, saying the funds were now coming through more of a variety of channels. Every year about US$200 million comes into Estonia from foreign investors.
"We take into consideration that the years of 1994 and 1995 ... were connected to a higher percentage of foriegn investment by privatisation," he said.
"Today ... foreign investment comes through share companies. That is the reason why there is less direct foreign investment in Estonia."
